CustomerSync.// RunAtTimeUtc: Daily run time in UTC, HH:mm format (e.g. '01:00' for 01:00 UTC). Leave empty to disable the scheduled run; the dev-only manual trigger endpoint still works regardless.
CustomerSync.// Source: Which feeder fills dbo.Customer / dbo.CustomerTradeUnit: 'ctrm' reads the Scoular GraphQL gateway; anything else (or EMPTY) reads the ODS views exactly as before. EMPTY here ON PURPOSE, same convention as Ctrm:Source (whose base doc reads 'EMPTY here ON PURPOSE so no environment can accidentally leave ODS') - each env opts in explicitly. Rollback = set the App Service setting CustomerSync__Source=ods; no redeploy.
CustomerSync.// MaxDeactivationPercent: Mass-deactivation guard, percent limit (0-100). A run aborts without writing when the customers or links it would deactivate exceed this percentage of the active total. The guard applies to BOTH sources; POST /api/diagnostics/customer-sync/run?force=true bypasses it for a legitimate mass change. GET /api/diagnostics/customer-sync/last-run shows whether the last run was aborted.
CustomerSync.// MaxDeactivationCount: Mass-deactivation guard, absolute row limit (>= 0). A run aborts without writing when more customers or links than this would be deactivated. Applies to both sources; ?force=true on POST /api/diagnostics/customer-sync/run bypasses it, and GET /api/diagnostics/customer-sync/last-run shows whether the last run was aborted.
CustomerSync.// DiscoveryWindowDays: CTRM source only: how many days back contract and ticket activity is scanned to discover producers the app does not hold yet (1-3660).
CustomerSync.// DiscoveryMaxPagesPerWindow: CTRM source only: page cap for each discovery window query (>= 1); hitting it marks the discovery truncated and is reported, never fatal.
CustomerSync.// CustomerLookupStrategy: CTRM source only: how the customer master is looked up by sourceCode. 'sourceCodes' (the default; anything but the literal 'aliased') sends one customers(sourceCodes:) list filter per chunk, paged 500 rows at a time - measured 2026-10-06: 100 codes in ~5 s. 'aliased' sends CustomerAliasCount aliased customers(sourceCode:) fields per request (~27 s per 20 codes with HC0045 timeouts). aliased is the fallback only; it, CustomersBySourceCodesAliased and CustomerAliasCount are deleted one PROD release after sourceCodes is verified (plan E7b).
CustomerSync.// SourceCodesMaxFilterChars: CTRM source only, sourceCodes strategy: budget for the ESTIMATED rendered filter of one request, at (code length + 9) characters per code (500-7000). The API rejects a filter over 7,000 encoded characters (VALIDATION 'The filter is too long') - the limit is on the rendered filter, not the number of values - so 6000 keeps a margin (~375 seven-character codes). If a run fails with 'sourceCodes filter too long', lower this.
CustomerSync.// SourceCodesMaxPerRequest: CTRM source only, sourceCodes strategy: most codes in one request regardless of length (1-1000); whichever of this and SourceCodesMaxFilterChars is reached first closes the chunk.
CustomerSync.// CustomerAliasCount: CTRM source only, aliased strategy (fallback): how many sourceCode lookups are aliased into one customers GraphQL request (1-50). Deleted with the aliased strategy in plan E7b.
CustomerSync.// CtrmConcurrency: CTRM source only: how many customer or activity requests run in parallel against the gateway (1-8).
CustomerSync.// CtrmSourceSystem: CTRM source only: optional sourceSystem argument added to the customers lookup. EMPTY = no filter.
CustomerSync.// CtrmExtendedFields: CTRM source only (plan E1): true adds merchandisingEmail, supplementalEmail, extendedPrimaryPhone, extendedAddressLine1-4, extendedCity, extendedStateProvince, extendedPostalCode, extendedCountry, nopidNo and paymentMethod to the customer lookup, and the sync then fills Email, SupplementalEmail, ExtendedPrimaryPhone, the Extended* address columns and NopIdNumber from CTRM (false = those columns keep their last ODS value; EffectiveStartDate/EffectiveEndDate are never written by CTRM), plus PaymentMethod (plan E2): on Source 'ctrm' the ACH badge reads dbo.Customer.PaymentMethod ('H' = ACH), which only this setting fills - with it off no producer shows ACH on ctrm (on ods the badge reads ODS base.Customer as before). FALSE here ON PURPOSE: an API that lacks any one of these fields answers HTTP 400 and the WHOLE lookup fails closed (CUSTOMER_SYNC_SCHEMA_MISMATCH, nothing written). Turn it on per environment only after GET /api/diagnostics/customer-sync/ctrm-capabilities lists every field there (nonprod did on 2026-10-06; PROD's API has not been checked); then GET /api/diagnostics/customer-sync/ctrm-probe should report ProjectionAccepted true. This knob stays (plan D15) - it is not a migration aid with a sunset.

AppAccess.// GroupId: Object id of the Entra access group, read DIRECTLY (GET /groups/{id}/...). The managed identity's group read is scoped to specific groups — it cannot list/search groups — so the id must be configured for deployed environments. EMPTY here ON PURPOSE: the base default fails open (unfiltered, diagnostic reports NotConfigured) so no environment can ever filter by the wrong group. Each env sets its OWN group in appsettings.{Env}.json — Development/Dev use the dev group, QA/Production use theirs. Once an env's GroupId is set AND its managed identity has the scoped-group read + User.ReadBasic.All grant, filtering activates automatically (no redeploy — the grant is AAD-side; cache refreshes within ~CacheMinutes).
AppAccess.// GroupName: Display label for the diagnostic, and the resolve-by-name fallback when GroupId is empty (name search only works under a developer credential locally — never as the scoped managed identity).
AppAccess.// CacheMinutes: How long a successful membership read is cached before Graph is asked again (failures are retried after ~5 minutes).

Ctrm.// Source: Which data source backs contract and ticket reads: 'ods' (or EMPTY) keeps every read on the ODS views exactly as before; 'ctrm' routes them at the Scoular.GraphQL API. EMPTY here ON PURPOSE so no environment can accidentally leave ODS - each env opts in via appsettings.{Env}.json. On 'ctrm' every contract and ticket read is CTRM: per-producer live, trade-unit-wide (Build-a-List, Actionable Insights, crop-year dashboard) via a cached producer-set read that mirrors the ODS flow (trade units -> producers in Origination -> CTRM). Only GetPricingLinesAsync (unused by the UI), farm and source-id lookups still delegate to ODS.
Ctrm.// GraphQlUri: Full URL of the GraphQL endpoint, e.g. https://apiqa.scoular.com/internal/graphql. Empty disables the CTRM path regardless of Source.
Ctrm.// TenantId: Entra tenant for the client-credentials token. Same tenant as AzureAd above.
Ctrm.// ClientId: App registration id used to call the CTRM API (client-credentials flow).
Ctrm.// Audience: Scope requested for the token, e.g. api://<api-app-id>/.default
Ctrm.// ClientSecret: NEVER set here. Supplied from Key Vault as secret 'Ctrm--ClientSecret' (Key Vault maps '--' to ':'), or omit entirely once the managed identity holds an app role on the CTRM API.
Ctrm.// PageSize: Rows per page when filling the contract snapshot. 500 is the API's observed ceiling; values above it are clamped.
Ctrm.// PageConcurrency: How many contract pages are fetched at once. Page 1 is fetched alone for its totalCount, which tells us the page count and frees the rest to run in parallel. A 500-row page with pricing lines costs ~10s, so this is the difference between a ~195s and a ~50s warm-up. Clamped to 1-8: a 429 from APIM fails the whole snapshot, so headroom matters more than the last few seconds.
Ctrm.// LiveCacheSeconds: How long a live per-producer read is reused, per projection. Selecting a producer triggers the contract list, the pacing card and the ticket read's open-contract set, which all want the same rows without pricing lines - this coalesces those into ONE core CTRM call. The pricing lines are a separate, more expensive read (they roughly double a contract page), so they get their own entry; a completed core read cannot satisfy them, but a completed FULL read does satisfy a core request. Keep it small (seconds): it exists to avoid duplicate round trips, not to cache data. Set 0 to disable.
Ctrm.// TradeUnitContractStrategy: How the trade-unit-wide contract read (Build-a-List, Insights, crop-year) fetches a producer set's full history. 'aliased' (default since 2026-09-24): the per-producer walk with the round trips collapsed - TradeUnitAliasCount x TradeUnitAliasCodesPerAlias producers per HTTP request as GraphQL aliases, each alias on the indexed path, fanned out at TradeUnitContractBatchConcurrency on a pool of its own; measured 4.7-8.3s / 59 requests for a 587-producer unit (10 producers per request, 16 in flight) with the identical 2,705 contracts the per-producer walk returns, against 36-73s / 587 requests one-per-call. A failed batch is retried once on singular aliases, and if it still fails the WHOLE read fails - never a shorter list. 'perProducer': one indexed contracts(customerId:) call per producer - the safe fallback the aliased strategy retries on, and the shape that measured 36-73s / 587 requests for the same unit (the code default if this key is missing). 'customerIds': the chunked 500-code list filter - the right shape once the API owner fixes its plan, but today every page is a ~25s server-side scan that trips the server's own 30s limit and never completed for that unit. Flip to 'customerIds' only after a probe shows a 500-code page under ~5s cold.
Ctrm.// TradeUnitAliasCount: How many aliases ride in ONE HTTP request when the strategy is 'aliased'; producers per request = this x TradeUnitAliasCodesPerAlias. Measured 2026-09-24 on a 587-producer unit, identical 2,705 contracts every run: 1 producer per call 62s/587 requests; 10 aliases x 2 codes (20 per request) 15-44s/30 requests at 6 in flight. The server resolves aliases one after another, so per-request time grows with the count: 20 per request put the slowest request at 20-23s LIVE on two units, near the 30s server cutoff (HC0045). 5 aliases x 2 codes (10 per request) at TradeUnitContractBatchConcurrency 16 measured 4.7-8.3s with the slowest request 7-9s - as fast as 20-per-request at the same concurrency, with three times the headroom. Fewer requests also spends less of the APIM rate quota, which is a volume budget.
Ctrm.// TradeUnitContractBatchConcurrency: How many batched contract requests are in flight at once - the aliased strategy's OWN cap, separate from TradeUnitMaxConcurrentRequests (which gates ticket pages) and from TradeUnitPerProducerConcurrency (the perProducer strategy). Measured 2026-09-24 on a healthy gateway, 10 producers per request, identical contract set, zero 429s: 6 in flight 38-44s; 12 in flight 6.8-15s; 16 in flight 4.7-8.3s. Re-measured 2026-09-29 on the same nonprod gateway in its slow phase, which is the day this setting has to survive: 16 at once failed the walk outright; a burst of 8 lost all 8 batches to HC0045 at ~36 s; a burst of 4 returned 4/4 with the slowest at 22 s, and a 1,271-producer trade unit then completed (128 batches, 140 s). The PROD gateway is a separate pool and absorbed 16 (15/16, the one loss a cold plan compile), so 8 is the default: half the burst, and with ServerTimeoutRetries=1 a cold batch is re-read from the server's cache rather than failed. The nonprod environments override this to 4 in their own files. Ask the API team what per-caller concurrency each pool is sized for before raising it. Clamped 1..32 in code; 8 is the code default. Read once at startup (CtrmTradeUnitThrottle) - an App Service setting change restarts the app, which is what applies it.
Ctrm.// TradeUnitAliasCodesPerAlias: 1 = each alias is the indexed singular customerId filter. 2 = each alias is a two-code customerIds list, which is measured safe (the list plan times out at three or more). 2 halves the request count again (30 vs 59 for the measured unit) and is the default; a batch that fails is automatically retried at 1 before the read is failed, so a regression in the list plan degrades to the slower shape rather than to an outage. Clamped to 1..2 in code.
Ctrm.// TradeUnitPerProducerConcurrency: Upper bound on concurrent per-producer calls in the perProducer strategy ONLY (the aliased strategy has its own cap, TradeUnitContractBatchConcurrency), applied BEFORE TradeUnitMaxConcurrentRequests - so the effective parallelism is the smaller of the two, 6 today. Kept as a separate dial so this strategy can be tuned without touching the shared background cap. Raising it past the shared cap has no effect.
Ctrm.// TradeUnitCacheMinutes: How long the trade-unit-wide CONTRACT read (contracts(customerIds:) full history for the producers in the selected trade units) is reused before it is refreshed. Refreshes never block: an expired entry is served to the caller while the refresh runs behind it, so this is how far behind CTRM a prompt can be, not how long anyone waits. Each refresh is a ~25s server-side scan per page (measured cold: 500 codes 24.7s), so keep this in tens of minutes - a 5-minute cadence per active trade-unit set was too much background load.
Ctrm.// TradeUnitContractConcurrency: How many contracts(customerIds:) pages run at once for one trade-unit read. Separate from PageConcurrency on purpose: every one of these pages is a ~25s server-side scan, and five at once alongside a ticket walk starved the server past the 110s client timeout on a 587-producer trade unit (2026-08-27). Two finishes reliably. Raise only after the API owner fixes the list-filter plan.
Ctrm.// TradeUnitMaxConcurrentRequests: Process-wide cap on BACKGROUND CTRM requests in flight at once - the trade-unit contract fan-out and the batched ticket pages, shared across both readers. Interactive per-producer reads (a click on the producer screen) never take a slot, which is the point: without this cap the trade-unit walk saturated the gateway and per-producer reads went from 1-2s to 13-18s (measured 2026-08-27). Raising it speeds the walk and slows clicks; lowering it does the reverse. 6 is the balance: a 587-producer trade unit warms in roughly a minute while clicks stay responsive.
Ctrm.// BackgroundMaxDeferSeconds: How long a background trade-unit request will wait for interactive reads (a producer selection) to finish before going ahead anyway. Background work yields to clicks because they share one gateway: with a walk running, a single producer ticket window measured 5-12s instead of its usual 1-3s (2026-08-27). Bounded so a busy app cannot starve the walk forever - Build-a-List still populates, just more slowly while people are clicking. 0 disables the priority rule and leaves only the concurrency cap.
Ctrm.// ServerTimeoutRetries: How many times a BACKGROUND page or batch that CTRM itself timed out (GraphQL error HC0045, "The request exceeded the configured timeout of 00:00:30", returned as HTTP 400) is re-sent, after ServerTimeoutRetryDelaySeconds. 1, as of 2026-09-29. It was 0 from 2026-09-03 because the server does not cancel a timed-out query (it runs to completion, 70s+), so a quick re-send only competed with the first copy - with the old 4 x 8s budget there were five copies of one query in flight by ~32s. That reasoning still holds for QUICK re-sends and is why the delay below is long. What changed: the API team documented (2026-09-28) that the slow phase is a fresh Db2 connection's one-time plan compile, ~25-31 s, right at the 30 s limit; the server then finishes the query and caches the result, so a re-send AFTER that window is served from cache. Measured on the PROD gateway 2026-09-29: the app's 10-producer batch cold = HC0045 at 31.5 s, the same batch re-sent later = 2.6 s. The API owner's own suggested shape (2026-09-03) was one retry after 90 s or none. One retry, 90 s, is that shape. Interactive reads keep their own budget (InteractiveServerTimeoutRetries). The code default is 0 so a missing key still fails safe.
Ctrm.// ServerTimeoutRetryDelaySeconds: Pause before a background HC0045 re-send. 90 s: long enough that the first copy has finished and been cached by the server (compile ~25-31 s, then the query itself), so the re-send reads the cache instead of competing. Shorter delays are what made retries harmful in 2026-09-03's measurements. Clamped 0..120 in code. Failure-path cost, for the record: a batch that times out twice now takes 30 + 90 + 30 s to fail, after which the walk stops sending (load-shedding) rather than retrying the remaining batches.
Ctrm.// InteractiveServerTimeoutRetries: HC0045 retry budget for a read a USER is waiting on (a producer selection). 0 ON PURPOSE (2026-09-03), same reason as ServerTimeoutRetries: the server keeps running the timed-out query, so a re-send 3s later competes with it and the user waits a second 30s for a slower answer. A click that hits HC0045 now fails at 30s and the screen shows the cached copy or the CTRM-unavailable state instead. Permanent for the same reason as ServerTimeoutRetries; the code default is 0 too. Per-producer reads measured 0 HC0045 in 791 calls on 2026-09-02, so this budget was rarely exercised.
Ctrm.// InteractiveServerTimeoutRetryDelaySec: Pause before an interactive HC0045 re-send. Unused while InteractiveServerTimeoutRetries is 0.
Ctrm.// InteractivePageConcurrency: How many ticket pages a single interactive read fetches at once. Unbounded, a nine-page window across three windows is twenty-seven simultaneous requests for one click, and the gateway was measured degrading at nine-way fan-out - the pages slow each other down. Background pages are bounded by TradeUnitMaxConcurrentRequests instead.
Ctrm.// InteractiveWindowSplit: Sub-divides each 366-day per-producer ticket window into this many contiguous parallel sub-windows. 1 = OFF, which is the default because the evidence conflicts: one probe run saw 3.4s -> 2.3s at 2-3 sub-windows, another saw four sub-windows do WORSE than one call (10.7s vs 7.3s). Contention is the variable, and splitting multiplies requests per click. Raise to 2 only after an A/B on /api/diagnostics/ctrm/producer-timing at 1 vs 2 under realistic load shows a win.
Ctrm.// TradeUnitContractMaxPagesPerChunk: Page cap (500 rows each) for one 500-producer chunk of the trade-unit-wide contract read. 100 = 50,000 contracts per chunk. The log says TRUNCATED when it is hit.
Ctrm.// TradeUnitTicketMaxPagesPerWindow: Page cap (500 rows each) for one 500-producer chunk of the trade-unit-wide TICKET read within one 366-day window. Per-producer reads keep a fixed cap of 10 because a single producer past 5,000 rows in one window means the filter is not applying; a 500-producer chunk legitimately runs to tens of thousands in the newest window. 200 = 100,000 rows per chunk-window. The log says TRUNCATED when it is hit.
Ctrm.// TicketLookbackDays: How far back the live per-producer ticket read reaches. 1095 = three years, matching the ODS cutoff, because the whole point of the CTRM path is to show the same population ODS does. The server caps a single bill-of-lading range at 366 days, so this is sliced into consecutive windows fetched in parallel and the cost is roughly the slowest window, not the sum: measured warm each window is ~1.0-1.3s, cold up to ~5.5s. Narrowing this is a latency dial that trades away older tickets - a producer's 2024 loads simply stop appearing - so change it deliberately.
Ctrm.// CrossBookedAppliedTickets: Adds a second, contract-scoped ticket read per producer that can see an applied ticket booked entirely under a DIFFERENT customer code. Off by default because it doubles the date scans, and a ticket read is charged by the scan: a producer with no tickets still costs ~3s for a 365-day window, so three years went from three scans to six and dominated a heavy producer's load (13.8s, measured 2026-08-27). The single customerId read still catches split loads on any header the producer appears on at all - only headers with NO detail for the producer are invisible to it, and a 90-producer sample in trade unit 2190 over a full year found zero of those. Turn ON if production data shows applied bushels on the contract disagreeing with the producer's ticket list.
Ctrm.// HistoricalTicketCacheMinutes: How long a ticket WINDOW that ended in the past is reused before it is refetched. The per-producer ticket read is three 366-day windows; the one containing today keeps LiveCacheSeconds because that is where new tickets land, but the two older ones hold tickets that rarely change and cost the most to fetch (~0.8-2.6s each against ~0.3-0.8s for the current year). So a repeat visit within this many minutes pays for the current window only. It is a bound on how stale an OLD ticket's status (a late settlement, a consolidation) can be on screen - not a promise that old tickets never change.
Ctrm.// TradeUnitCurrentWindowCacheMinutes: How long the TRADE-UNIT-WIDE ticket read's current window (the one containing today) is reused. Separate from LiveCacheSeconds on purpose: at 60 seconds the current window's refresh - a full 366-day chunk scan of the whole trade unit, 5-15 pages of 500 - re-ran roughly every minute while anyone used ticket prompts, competing with producer clicks for the same gateway slots. This bounds how long a brand-new ticket can take to appear in a Build-a-List PROMPT; the producer screen has its own read on LiveCacheSeconds and is unaffected. Stale-while-revalidate still applies, so nobody waits on the refresh.
Ctrm.// ServeClickFromTradeUnitCache: Whether a producer CLICK may be answered from the warm trade-unit producer-set caches (the rows the home page already fetched for Build-a-List) instead of waiting on live CTRM calls. The rows are the same projections and rules a live read returns, filtered to the producer; the live read is ALWAYS kicked behind the answer and the client silently re-reads seconds later, so the screen converges to live either way - this only removes the 2-14s first-paint wait. False = every click waits on CTRM, exactly the pre-2026-08-28 behaviour.
Ctrm.// ServeClickFromTradeUnitCacheMaxMinute: How old a trade-unit CONTRACT set may be and still answer a click's first paint. Bounded by TradeUnitCacheMinutes in practice (the set refreshes itself on that cadence); this is the hard ceiling for serving clicks from it. Ticket windows use their own expiries instead (TradeUnitCurrentWindowCacheMinutes for today's window), so a click's tickets are never staler than a Build-a-List prompt's.
Ctrm.// KeepWarmMinutes: Cadence of the background keep-warm cycle that re-runs the trade-unit reads for recently-used producer sets, so their stale-while-revalidate refreshes happen on the clock instead of on a user's prompt. 0 disables the cycle. Runs only while Ctrm:Source is 'ctrm'; reads go through the background throttle and yield to clicks.
Ctrm.// KeepWarmForHours: How long after its last use a producer set keeps being maintained by the keep-warm cycle. Past this, the set goes cold until the next home-page load touches it again. 2 covers the case this exists for - someone returning from a meeting to a page they left open - without refreshing a trade unit nobody is looking at for the rest of the day, which is load on the CTRM gateway for nothing. Raise it only if testers report cold prompts after long gaps.
Ctrm.// KeepWarmFailureBackoffMinutes: How long the keep-warm cycle leaves a producer set alone after one of its reads failed, instead of re-walking it on the next 5-minute cycle. Added 2026-09-28 after the nonprod gateway's slow phase: every timed-out query keeps running on the database to completion (70 s+, per the API team), so re-sending 59 batched contract requests plus retries, then the ticket walk, every 5 minutes for every set in use, kept the database saturated and turned a slow phase into an evening of 503s. The caches keep their last good copy meanwhile, and a user's own request is never gated by this. Minimum 1.
Ctrm.// RecentTicketDays: How far back the recent-unapplied ticket read looks — the one behind Actionable Insights > Spot Loads. 30 matches the cutoff the ODS query used, so leave it there in any environment whose output is being compared against ODS. It is configurable only because 30 days makes the read unverifiable in nonprod: dev CTRM has no ticket activity in the last 30 days for the real producer population (the same ten producers return 0 rows over 30 days and 834 over a year), so Spot Loads renders empty whichever source backs it. Widening this is the only way to prove the path end to end without waiting for data. A wider window is not a data difference — it is a different question.

UsageDashboard.// ExclusionManagers: Short names (UPN before the @) of the IT users allowed to see and manage the usage-dashboard exclusion list. Enforced server-side on the excluded-users/access-users endpoints (on top of AdminOnly); the client hides the gear icon for everyone else. Base list applies to every environment unless overridden in appsettings.{Env}.json.
UsageDashboard.// ViewAll: MOVED OUT OF CONFIG. Who may read the WHOLE organisation and pick an arbitrary manager from the dropdown now lives in the dbo.UsageDashboardViewAllUsers table, so the list can be changed with a plain SQL INSERT/DELETE -- no redeploy and no App Service restart (see scripts/Manage-UsageDashboardViewAll.sql). Rationale and fail-closed behaviour are documented on the UsageDashboardViewAllUser entity and UsageDashboardViewAllProvider.

SecurityHeaders.// SpaConnectSrcHosts: Specific hosts allowed in the SPA CSP connect-src (in addition to 'self' + Microsoft login/graph). Set per environment (appsettings.{Env}.json) to that env's own App Service host — replaces the former *.azurewebsites.net wildcard. Empty here so local dev relies on 'self' + localhost.
